findings.fix: Make the reference/value and footprint agree: use a resistor footprint for R parts, a capacitor footprint for C parts, and regenerate the BOM from the corrected design.
findings.what: R1 is a R designator on a C chip land 'Capacitor_SMD:C_0805_2012Metric'. Same 0805 chip size, so the part fits; the land is the generic capacitor variant. Rename the footprint to the resistor land if the BOM tooling keys on it
findings.why: The reference designator tells the BOM and assembly process what kind of part this is, while the footprint points at a different passive family. The board may route electrically, but the assembly house can load the wrong bin or stop for clarification.

findings.fix: If the regulator rings at load steps, add 11.8 µF directly from '+3V3' to ground at the regulator.
findings.what: A sourced operating condition is violated on U3, C3, C6 and C9 at net "+3V3". U3 (AMS1117-3.3) output '+3V3' has 10.2 µF from output to ground (C3 100 nF, C6 10 µF, C9 100 nF), below the 22 µF card 'ams1117_3v3' records as the datasheet's recommendation for loop stability (a recommended value, not a stated minimum, so this is a note, not a fault). The datasheet's 22 µF is solid tantalum: stability depends on the capacitor's type and ESR, which the board does not record. Remedy: If the regulator rings at load steps, add 11.8 µF directly from '+3V3' to ground at the regulator.
findings.why: The model card quotes the part's recommended operating table and compares it with the full rail range the board can present. A nominal point inside the table is not enough when a battery or regulator tolerance crosses a published bound.

sections.verdict: INCONCLUSIVE: 2 current-carrying / active part(s) have no model (Q1, U4), so a clean result here is not a clean bill. Draft models from their datasheets (`hauksbee models extract --unmodelled <board>`, or the Extend button in `hauksbee serve`), scaffold one by hand (`hauksbee models new`, then --models-dir), or supply BOM identity (--bom) to make this verdict conclusive.
